PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Undoubtedly Ferrari’s most significant and eagerly awaited car of the 2010s, the LaFerrari brought Ferrari boldly into the future as it would be the marque’s first hybrid hypercar. Mating Ferrari’s traditional V-12 engine alongside an electric motor made for a truly incredible driving experience, one which continues to influence Ferrari’s current models to this day. Needless to say, numerous lessons were learned in the LaFerrari’s development, and it can be argued that the development of this car was more important than the development of any other car in Ferrari’s recent history., Dubbed internally as project code “F150,” the research and testing phases of the supercar’s progression were divided into three cycles. The car offered here was internally designated “M6” and was the first test mule for this project. Built on the basis of Ferrari’s existing Type F142 platform, the 458 Italia, M6 bears much likeness to the 458 cosmetically, with the later prototypes appearing much more visually similar to the production-ready LaFerrari. Although the LaFerrari was built on a carbon fiber tub, M6 would utilize the 458’s aluminum chassis which was modified to fit a V-12 Type F140EB engine. Engineers also adapted the shock tower around the prototype as part of their research into weight distribution of the car., Offered for sale alongside a number of exterior panels that it wore during factory testing, it’s important to note that the car is accompanied by a factory-issued “Yellow Binder” Attestato per vetture Serie speciale. This yellow binder outlines the car’s usage by Ferrari. First built up by Ferrari between February and April of 2012, from May 2012 to March 2013 the car was used for developing the brake systems. This testing was undertaken entirely at Ferrari’s own Fiorano circuit from June to September of 2013. The binder further outlines that the car was used for development of the suspension, brakes, steering, and tires for the LaFerrari as well as being the LaFerrari prototype first fitted with the LaFerrari-specific Electronic Stability Program (ESP) system., Once LaFerrari production was well underway and all the production cars had been allocated, Ferrari began to offer its LaFerrari development mules for sale once it was clear that they were no longer required for testing. This example, sold to its first private owner in July 2016, was offered subject to a refresh and repaint by Ferrari, on the understanding that the car was not homologated, therefore could not be registered for road use nor be used on public race circuits. However, this very collectable part of Ferrari history could be used on private land with its running powertrain. Furthermore, it is important to note that upon a successful sale, a service will be carried out by Carrozzeria Zanasi in Maranello to ensure the car is in running and driving order, with these costs covered by the consignor., Today, over a decade since M6 was lapping Fiorano all in the pursuit of developing Ferrari’s next hypercar, this prototype is a fascinating part of not only the history of the LaFerrari, but the history of the numerous hybrid models that would follow in its footsteps. Thus, this is a car that would stand proud within any collection of Maranello’s latest and greatest supercars.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The Ferrari 599 GTO carries the Gran Turismo Omologata name, the same three words previously used for the 250 GTO and the 288 GTO. Gran Turismo Omologata translates to ‘Grand Touring Homologated,’ a designation given to road-legal cars built to homologate a series of racing cars. In a similar vein, the 599 GTO is the roadgoing sibling of the Ferrari 599XX, created by translating the XX program’s lessons in aerodynamics, chassis calibration, braking, and powertrain to public roads., Commissioned by a female client in Greece as recorded by the original service book, this 599 GTO began life as a fully bespoke Atelier order. The consultation, approval, and build cycle for an Atelier commission was more involved and time-consuming than a standard order at the time. The dedication plate itself is a wonderful detail. It is hand-engraved in the original client’s own handwriting with the words “To myself Maria,” and it is positioned on the lower dashboard to the left of the steering wheel. The car was delivered new via Genesis S.A., the official Ferrari dealer just north of Athens in July 2011. In a recent conversation with Genesis S.A., they confirmed that Maria decided to leave the car in storage at the showroom, and it was never driven by her., The specification announces itself at first glance. Rubino Micalizzato is classified as an “Extracampionario,” special order multilayer Ferrari paint color that rewards close viewing. In soft light it reads as deep red to burgundy. In direct sun it opens up with brighter ruby highlights and a metallic undertone that reveals a gold to bronze sparkle within the flake. The roof is finished in Grigio Silverstone Opaco. It is believed that the carbon Scuderia shields, an expensive Ferrari Genuine after-sales accessory, were installed by the delivering dealer, and sit on the front wings matching the center caps in carbon so that every exterior detail is in harmony., Inside, the car goes well beyond the standard palette. Blu Scuro Alcantara covers the entire cabin, including seats, steering wheel, dashboard, doors, and lower/upper trim, specified as an Extracampionario selection. The seat belts are Bordeaux rather than bright red, a great choice that ties the interior to the depth of the exterior. The rev counter is red. A factory-fitted roll bar speaks to the GTO’s intent. The result is truly spectacular to behold and boasts a level of specification that few, if any other examples, duplicate., After four years remaining at Genesis S.A. in Greece, Maria sold the 599 GTO to a private collector in Germany in 2015 and was road registered there that same year. With that owner, it was used sparingly, explaining the very low mileage and the exceptional originality evident upon inspection., Mechanically, the 599 GTO stands apart from the 599 GTB. The V-12 engine shares its F140 architecture with the Enzo yet benefits from the lessons of the XX program. Breathing was reworked, internal losses reduced, calibration refined, and maximum output quoted at 670 horsepower. The exhaust side is central to the car’s character. The 599 GTO uses 6 into 1 manifolds derived from the 599XX, flowing into a freer system that gives an unmistakable noise. Many consider it amongst the best-sounding modern Ferraris. The gearbox was tuned for shifts measured in around sixty milliseconds, a response that makes the car feel alive in the driver’s hands. The balance of aerodynamic revision and weight reduction completes the transformation so that the 599 GTO feels razor sharp while retaining a grand touring breadth., The 599 GTO was limited to 599 examples worldwide. It is therefore rarer than the F12tdf with 799 built and rarer than the 812 Competizione coupe at 999 constructed. Adding to this example’s allure, Ferrari’s current Tailor Made program was not available for the 599 GTO and the only route to a fully bespoke configuration was via the Atelier program. Very few GTOs were processed at this level. Among those few, surely examples with lower mileage than this example, 1,552 km at the time of cataloguing, are exceptionally scarce. In today’s market, with high levels of factory customization being of utmost importance, few 599 GTOs will be as compelling to collectors as this example, especially when taking its low mileage into consideration. It still rides on its original factory-supplied Michelin Pilot Super Sport tires, a detail that underlines the minimal use., It is important to note that the car is accompanied by two keys, its original owner’s manuals with pouch, tool kit, tire inflator kit, radio code card, white maintenance gloves, and its Classiche certification binder confirming its sensational specification (which was delivered with the car when new). Further accompanying the car are two service tags from Maranello Service, the official Ferrari service center in Madrid, showing services in 2020 and 2023 at 1,348 km and 1,447 km respectively. Importantly, the car is currently undergoing an annual service at Autoropa Stockholm, the official Ferrari dealer and service centre located in Stockholm, Sweden., Having established itself as a modern-day classic from the moment it was announced, the 599 GTO combines incredible performance with welcome practicality, leaving for a car that revels in spirited driving yet one that can be easily driven on a regular basis or for longer journeys. This particular example’s specification reflects that dual-purpose personality. Offered with less than 1,600 km, this is a truly remarkable example that should not be overlooked, and one would be hard pressed to find a more impressive example anywhere worldwide.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Inspired by Mercedes-Benz’s iconic 300 SLR, the car which drove Stirling Moss and co-driver Denis Jenkinson to a record-breaking victory in the 1955 Mille Miglia, the SLR McLaren Stirling Moss sought to bring the performance and personality of the 300 SLR into the 21st century, making for the most radical roadgoing automobile Mercedes-Benz had built since the CLK GTR Roadster., Taking things a touch further than the already exceptional SLR McLaren, the Stirling Moss’ restyled carbon body panels and lack of windscreen and roof helped it to shed some 200 kilograms over the standard SLR McLaren. This allowed for a 3.5-second launch to 100 km/h alongside a claimed 354 km/h top speed. When Car magazine road-tested the car in 2009, they likened the experience of full-throttle acceleration to ‘standing on the wingtip of a 747’ and cited the performance achievable only by those ‘whose neck muscles can bear it.’, This was no automobile for the faint-hearted, and only seventy-five examples would be built, all destined for VIP Mercedes-Benz customers. The vast majority of SLR McLaren Stirling Moss production was finished in Crystal Laurite Silver Metallic over a Silver Arrow 300 SL Red leather interior, recalling the color scheme of that record-breaking 300 SLR: Silver with a splash of red paint for the racing numbers, making for a sensational visual contrast. However, a handful of other colors were available., It is believed that only four SLR McLaren Stirling Moss’ were finished in Designo Mystic White from the factory, with two of those cars being sold new to the collections of two separate royal families in the Middle East. This example was built to EU specifications for delivery to Germany and has enjoyed just two registered owners since new. Having been driven less than 60 kilometers from new, it is presented in virtually as-new condition throughout, exceptionally well preserved as a remarkable example of one of Mercedes-Benz’s most exciting automobiles. It is presented with a host of original accessories, including two leather driving helmets, two Oakley SLR Stirling Moss-specific driving goggles, as well as protective cases for the driver and passenger tonneau covers, a cover for the wind deflector, and a silver painted blank wind deflector panel for the passenger side., While ‘speedster-style’ supercars are now seemingly commonplace today, with companies such as Ferrari, McLaren, and Aston Martin all having had their own take on that theme, it was the SLR McLaren Stirling Moss that kick-started this trend in the 21st century. With only seventy-five examples built, these are exceptionally rare cars already, with the cars originally finished in colors other than silver being even more desirable. With most of these locked away within long-term collections, this represents a remarkable opportunity to acquire a nearly-new example in a spectacular and seldom-seen color scheme.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: As a true marvel of 21st century automotive performance, perhaps the best way to understand the SF90 XX Spider is to take in its performance figures. A sprint to 62 mph from a standstill is accomplished in just 2.3 seconds, leading to 125 mph in just 6.7 seconds and finally a top speed of 200 mph. The SF90 XX Spider’s hybrid powertrain, consisting of a 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine assisted by three electric motors (two at the front axle and one located between the engine and the gearbox at the rear), produces an incredible 1,013 bhp., Built with the ethos of the incredible 599 XX, FXX, and FXX K, yet able to be driven on the open road unlike its XX predecessors, this is an unrelenting performance machine capable of outpacing almost any other car in existence. The rarest model within the SF90 family, only 599 examples will be produced by Ferrari, making it rarer than its closed sibling., Offered from its second owner, this SF90 XX Spider boasts a remarkable specification with numerous carbon fiber options and details, further reflecting its lightweight nature. Delivered new via Ferrari of Beverly Hills just last year, the car was beautifully specified via Ferrari’s Tailor Made department. Finished in Nero DS 1250, the car’s menacing body is offset by glossy red carbon fiber and Bordeaux Alcantara throughout, making for a sporty yet sinister appearance., Red carbon fiber can be seen throughout the exterior of the car, starting from the front splitter and trim underneath the headlights, continuing to the ducts in the nose including all the carbon fiber trim underneath the front compartment, and moving to the rear of the car with the engine vents, rear spoiler, and rear diffuser all trimmed in glossy red carbon to match. The SF90 XX Spider’s interior is trimmed in a mix of Nero and Bordeaux Alcantara to match the exterior livery., Further to the incredible color combination, the car is extraordinarily well outfitted in terms of optional extras, and is fitted with the AFS system, airbrushed Scuderia shields, brake calipers painted black, activation of the MyFerrari Connect mobile app, black tailpipes, cabin-mounted fire extinguisher, the advanced front driving camera, and diamond-polished forged wheels amongst other options., Not all SF90 XX Spiders have been completed or delivered, making the opportunity to acquire this example especially tantalizing as it can now be sold free of restrictions. With the 849 Testarossa having recently been announced to replace the SF90, there’s no doubt that the SF90 XX Spider will be the most desirable variant of the SF90 family of Ferraris, offering limited production exclusivity, track-focused performance, and in the case of this example, low mileage and a sensational specification.
